content.todaysFocus: Day 60 lands in the easy stretch between the colic peak and the 4-month sleep regression. Avi tracks fluidly now and engages more, so it is the right week to upgrade the book rotation from pure high-contrast to narrative and tactile pages.

actionItems.body: Add two texture or simple-narrative board books to the rotation today, keeping one or two high-contrast favorites in the mix. Tactile pages now recruit touch alongside vision, and reading aloud is one of the highest-effect-size inputs for later expressive vocabulary.
Hold the 2-month visit's six vaccines as the baseline and confirm the 4-month visit is on the calendar, window day 112-126, when RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2 are due.
Run a 2-4 hour daycare or nanny trial this week if you are returning to work soon, since standard 12-week US leave ends in roughly two to three weeks and you want the handoff tested before it counts.

watchFors: [low concern] Lingering low-grade fussiness up to about 72 hours after the 2-month shots, and spit-up volume tapering as the upper esophageal sphincter matures.
[monitor] Asymmetric movement or a persistent head turn to one side suggesting torticollis; document which side and raise it at the 4-month visit.
[call within 24h] Persistent vomiting unrelated to vaccines, a new heart murmur, or a clear drop in wet-diaper output.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher in an infant under 90 days, blue lips, or labored breathing warrant a same-day call now, and 911 for blue lips.

enrichment.body: Graduate the rotation from purely high-contrast cards to texture board books and simple narrative, letting him pat and mouth the tactile pages so touch and vision work together.
Sing live across varied tempos, a slow lullaby into a fast clapping song and back, while his tempo discrimination is sharpening; varied input preserves perceptual range.

Hold coo conversations in extended turns, answering each vocalization and pausing two to three seconds for his reply; vowel-consonant combinations like goo are starting, and conversational turns predict later language outcomes.
Keep cumulative tummy time at 60-plus minutes a day in short bouts, placing a toy just out of reach to motivate stretching and forearm push-ups.

upcoming: Day 56-70 (now): 2-month well visit window, with HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, and IPV #1 if not yet done.
Day 57-72 (now): post-vaccine 24-72h window for low-grade fever, drowsiness, and fussiness.
Day 112-126: 4-month well visit, with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2.

content.todaysFocus: Around now Avi begins turning attention toward his own name and holding back-and-forth coo exchanges. The week's job is to feed that reciprocity, since conversational turns, not raw word count, are what predict later language outcomes.

actionItems.body: Say his name warmly during awake-alert windows and watch for the orienting turn; then respond to each coo as if he spoke, pause two to three seconds, and answer again. Conversational turns drive Broca's-area development independent of total word count.
Confirm the 4-month visit is scheduled, window day 112-126, where RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2 are due; the rotavirus series has hard age cutoffs, so do not let it drift.
Start a loose first-birthday plan now if you want a specific SF or NYC venue, since top venues book six to nine months out and putting the date down prevents calendar collisions with family visits.

watchFors: [low concern] Quiet startle to loud sounds and wet sneezing during the day; both are routine and need no action.
[monitor] No social smile by this point; note it and raise it at the next well visit rather than waiting.
[call within 24h] A run of refused feeds in a row, or new color changes during feeds.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, an apnea pause, or seizure-like activity needs a call now, and 911 for blue lips or labored breathing.

enrichment.body: Use his name and warm parentese in serve-and-return turns, pausing for his reply; back-and-forth cooing is consolidating and the turn-taking is the active ingredient, not the volume.
Vary the tummy-time surface across the day, a firm mat, your lap, then a slight Boppy incline, to keep cumulative prone time above 60 minutes and build neck and upper-body strength.
Take a carrier walk outside with his chin off his chest and face visible, giving him upright sensory input and the parent some cardiovascular recovery.

upcoming: Day 57-72 (now): tail of the post-vaccine window; lingering low-grade fussiness is still expected.
Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens near three months; start anchoring a consistent sleep-wake routine.
Day 112-126: 4-month well visit, with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2.

subject: Day 62: plan a Botanical Garden loop

content.todaysFocus: Day 62 closes out week nine, the calm post-vaccine stretch. A low-stimulation outdoor outing fits the moment: it gives Avi varied sensory input and the parents daylight and movement without overloading him.

actionItems.body: Plan a quiet stroller loop through the SF Botanical Garden for a weekday this week, mid-morning before crowds, packing a sun hat and one feed's worth of milk; greenery and dappled light are exactly the low-key sensory variety he can handle now.

Keep vitamin D supplementation at 400 IU per day for breastfed or predominantly breastfed infants regardless of how much outdoor time he gets; sun exposure does not replace the supplement at this age.
Lock the 4-month visit on the calendar, window day 112-126, for RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2.

watchFors: [low concern] Brief fussing when the stroller stops moving, and squinting in bright light; shade the canopy and keep moving.
[monitor] Spit-up that is forceful or paired with arching during feeds rather than the usual easy posset; document frequency for the next visit.
[call within 24h] A clear drop in wet diapers over a day, or a new murmur noted by anyone examining him.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, blue lips, or labored breathing means call now, and 911 for blue lips.

enrichment.body: Plan a calm stroller loop through the SF Botanical Garden for greenery, fresh air, and gentle sensory variety, keeping the outing short and the canopy shaded.
Let him track leaves and dappled light moving overhead, recline the stroller slightly so the moving pattern fills his visual field and feeds smooth tracking.
Hum a calm tune as you walk the paths, pairing your live voice with the new setting; participatory singing, not recorded background, is what carries the benefit.

upcoming: Day 57-72 (now): final days of the post-vaccine window; mild lingering fussiness still counts as low concern.
Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens; begin a consistent dim-after-sunset routine.
Day 112-126: 4-month well visit, with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2.

content.todaysFocus: Week 10 opens, and many infants produce their first true laugh in the 10-14 week range. Social reciprocity is sharpening fast, so this week is about playing for that laugh and answering every chuckle.

actionItems.body: Play exaggerated peek-a-boo and gentle tickle games during his most alert window and watch for the first laugh, which commonly emerges between 10 and 14 weeks; some infants wait until 14-16 weeks, which is still normal.
Begin tracking sleep windows this week, logging last wake, time he fell asleep, and nap length; the pattern stabilizes enough by 12-14 weeks to anchor a loose schedule before the 4-month regression.
Book a 100-day or 3-month photo session now if you want one, since week 12-14 is the window and the better photographers are scheduling weeks out.

watchFors: [low concern] Profuse drooling and hand-sucking, which reflect salivary-gland maturation rather than teething; first teeth typically arrive at 6-10 months.
[monitor] Persistent head asymmetry or flattening on one side; reposition during sleep and held time and flag at the next visit if it does not respond.
[call within 24h] Decreased feeding lasting more than 24 hours, or any new color change during feeds.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, an apnea pause, or seizure-like activity needs a call now, and 911 for blue lips.

enrichment.body: Play exaggerated peek-a-boo and light tummy raspberries face-to-face to elicit early laughs, repeating the gag that lands; the surprise-and-resolution structure is what tips a coo into a chuckle.
Cheer and answer every chuckle to extend the back-and-forth, treating each sound as a turn and pausing for his next one; the reciprocity is what builds later language.
Add one new book this week alongside the repeats at roughly a 3:1 repeat-to-novel ratio, which balances prosodic familiarity against lexical novelty.

upcoming: Day 70-76: confirm caregivers and grandparents are current on Tdap before more contact, since pertussis is the contact-borne illness most dangerous to infants.
Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens near three months; start a consistent sleep-wake routine.
Day 112-126: 4-month well visit, with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2.

content.todaysFocus: Avi is bringing hands to mouth and starting to swipe at what he sees. Day 64 leans into early cause and effect: putting a sound-making object where his own motion produces a result he can notice.

actionItems.body: Place a light rattle in his hand or set a kick-piano at his feet during alert play so his own movement makes the sound, which is the first cause-and-effect link and motivates more deliberate reaching and kicking.

Confirm that caregivers, grandparents, and any nanny are up to date on Tdap, flu, and COVID-19 before increased contact; pertussis from an adult contact is the vaccine-preventable illness most likely to be fatal to an infant.
Keep logging sleep windows so a loose schedule is ready to anchor by 12-14 weeks, ahead of the 4-month regression.

watchFors: [low concern] Hands-to-mouth and gumming on fists; this is normal oral and motor exploration, not a feeding problem.
[monitor] Hands that stay persistently fisted without opening, or movement that consistently favors one side; document and raise at the next visit.
[call within 24h] A new feeding-refusal pattern, or a fever onset you are tracking that has not yet crossed the rectal threshold.
[call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, blue lips, labored breathing, or seizure-like activity means call now, and 911 for blue lips.

enrichment.body: Put a light rattle in his hand or a kick-piano at his feet so his action makes a sound, building the earliest sense that his own movement causes a result.
Connect those cause-and-effect sounds to your varied live singing, echoing the rattle's beat in a quick clapping tune so the self-made sound ties into participatory music.
Narrate the cause and effect out loud as it happens, naming what he just did in warm parentese and pausing for his reply, so the new motor discovery doubles as a conversational turn.

upcoming: Day 70-76: confirm caregiver Tdap and start a small freezer milk stash if you are returning to work.
Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens; dim the lights after sunset to seed the routine.
Day 112-126: 4-month well visit, with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, and IPV #2.
